newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ minister says jobs data should lend confidence.
newsitem.headline: NZ minister says jobs data should lend confidence.

text.p: New Zealand's Minister of Employment Peter McCardle said on Tuesday it was not surprising that official unemployment in the June quarter had risen, given the economic indicators that existed several months ago.

Earlier Statistics New Zealand reported a headline unemployment rate of 6.7 percent, lower than average market expectations of 6.9 percent, and an increase in the number of hours worked of 2.5 percent.

"New Zealand can continue to take confidence in the fact that today's 6.7 percent result still puts our official unemployment rate clearly lower than the OECD average of 7.3 percent and ninth out of the 21 OECD countries with comparable surveys," he said in a statement.

The government's priorities over this term continued to be on fostering strong economic growth, while targeting what he called "stubborn" long-term unemployment statistics that have been seen since the late 1980s, he said.
